title: Lewis Hamilton says ‘Israel’s genocide in Gaza is appalling’ after Rafah visit
author: Agencies and Guardian sport
text:
F1 driver urges Israel to let aid into Gaza

Trip involved tour of facilities with aid workers

Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton said on Wednesday that Israel must allow aid ⁠trucks into Gaza, a day after he visited the Rafah border crossing in Egypt.

Hamilton, a seven-time ⁠world champion, arrived ⁠in ​El Arish on Tuesday, where he was briefed on how aid is prepared and coordinated before it ⁠is sent into Gaza , as he toured the Rafah crossing and the Egyptian Red Crescent’s aid warehouses.

He has frequently posted on social media about children killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza and called for a ceasefire. A ceasefire agreement reached last year has halted major combat operations in Gaza, but the amount of aid reaching the territory continues to fall far short of the agreed-upon minimum of 600 trucks a day.

“The past ⁠three years of Israel’s genocide in Gaza is appalling. It’s an ​injustice for people to ‌be denied their freedom, ‌their safety and their dignity. No human being should be treated ‌as though their life matters less,” the Ferrari driver wrote on Instagram.

Israel strongly denies accusations of genocide and says its military campaign in Gaza targets Hamas militants.

Hamilton described seeing food trucks lined up and ready to go at the border that were ‌regularly held up or faced major delays.

“I saw walls stretching for miles, built to keep them in. Standing there, outside what felt like an open-air prison, all I could think about was getting in to help,” he said in the post. “At the Rafah border, I saw food trucks lined up ready to go, but they’re regularly not allowed in or face major delays. The first driver in line that I spoke to had already been waiting over 12 hours. At the nearby logistics centre, I saw the hard work of the aid workers, but I also saw what gets rejected for crazy reasons. Sleeping bags, first aid kits, medical equipment, wheelchairs even footballs for kids.

“Israel needs to fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire and let the aid trucks in. I know so many people feel that same helplessness. That same need to do something rather than just watch. No excuse. I don’t want ⁠us to get used to their suffering. I don’t ​want us to ​look away.”

Hamilton, 41, is an ​advocate for humanitarian causes. In 2021 he founded ​Mission 44, a ‌charity that supports ​young people ​and works to improve their access to education and employment.

“I think we need to make sure we’re pushing to free Congo, free Sudan, free Syria, free Palestine ,” Hamilton said last month. “I think there’s a lot of peace that I’m hoping we get to at some stage.”

At the crossing on Tuesday, Hamilton greeted aid workers with “Assalamu alaikum” a widely used Arabic greeting meaning “peace be upon you”. He shook hands and briefly spoke to workers and officials.

Hamilton is fourth in the drivers’ championship. Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli has won the title with three races to go. The Las Vegas Grand Prix is 21 November before the Qatar Grand Prix on 29 November and the season-ending Abu Dhabi Grand Prix on 6 December.

title: Life Time Grand Prix Increases Prize Purse by Over $200K
author: Will Tracy
text:
The Life Time Grand Prix prize purse is increasing significantly in 2027. (Photo: Life Time)

Racers in the Life Time Grand Prix can look forward to bigger pay days in 2027.

Life Time announced Thursday that the premier off-road race series in North America will have an $800,000 USD prize purse in 2027, a 36 percent increase over 2026’s $590,000 purse. The move signals continued growth for the series and an investment in its athletes as it heads into its sixth season.

“One of the things we’re trying to do is kind of fundamentally change the business model of professional cycling,” Kimo Seymour, president, events and media at Life Time, told Velo .

“Athletes don’t get an opportunity to participate in the success of the events. And it’s no secret how broken the whole pure sponsorship model of professional cycling is.

“I’m like, well, why can’t we change it a little bit? If we can generate more revenue, we ought to be able to figure out a way to share more of that revenue with the athletes. I think it is a way for us to give back some of the success we’re seeing with the series.”

Payouts have increased for each of the seven individual races in the series, which runs from April to October, as well as for most of the top finishers overall in the series. Of the $800,000 purse, half is dedicated to payouts for the individual races, and the other half to the top overall finishers in the series.

As has been the case since the series’ first year in 2022, the money will be split equally between the men’s and women’s fields, totaling $400,000 to each.

Unbound Gravel and Leadville continue to have the largest prize purses in the series, growing from $60,000 per race to $80,000. Life Time is substantially increasing the prize money for Big Sugar, the final race of the series, raising it from $30,000 to $80,000. It signals the race’s growth and increased importance.

“Our feeling was that Big Sugar is, for lack of a better term, it’s just getting bigger and bigger each year,” Seymour said. “It’s an important one on the calendar for the Grand Prix. We’re getting more and more non-Grand Prix pro athletes showing up at that event as well.”

The remaining races in the series—Sea Otter Classic, Chequamegon MTB Festival, The Rad Dirt Fest and Little Sugar MTB—will pay $40,000 per race. That’s up from $30,000 for all those events excluding The Rad, which sees its payout increase significantly from $5,000 as it returns to the Life Time Grand Prix in 2027.

The payouts at individual races now run deeper into the results sheet, to 10th place overall, up from the top five spots in 2026. Depending on the race, individual race winners will earn the same $10,000 or $5,000 prizes as in 2026, with bigger paydays spread across the remaining top 10 athletes.

The top-two overall finishers in the series will see their winnings reduced from $50,000 to $40,000 and $33,000 to $30,000, while spots 3-10 will see their winnings increase by at least a few thousands dollars per position.

Many of these decisions on how to distribute the prize purse have come from the athletes themselves, Seymour said.

“We got a lot of great feedback from the athletes and spreading the prize purse at the individual events down 10 deep was one of their suggestions,” he said. “And then also spreading it a little more equitably in the top 10 overall in the Grand Prix was another suggestion that came from the athletes.”

Life Time’s expenses for the series are about an even split between prize money and the costs of producing and promoting the events, said Seymour. Life Time has opted to continue to keep that investment equal as the series grows, seeing value in investing in the athletes who also help drive the media impressions that grow the series.

Seymour envisions the Life Time Grand Prix possibly reaching a point where it can create a revenue sharing model of sorts, more akin to one of the major North American sports leagues than traditional cycling models as we currently know them.

“At some point, that’s my dream, is that we would get [to revenue sharing],” he said. “We do that to some extent where now we’re paying all athletes that finish the series.”

Racers outside the top-10 overall but who finish the series in 2027 will get $2,500, continuing the finisher bonus that the series introduced in 2026.

title: MotoGP makes major US TV step with ESPN deal
author: Simon Patterson
text:
MotoGP has penned a new two-year deal for 2027 with broadcaster ESPN that will finally give the series a more permanent United States TV home, after a series of somewhat confusing contracts in recent seasons jumping around between different channels, platforms, and broadcasters.

The new deal, which will cover coverage not just in the US but also across Latin America, means ESPN becomes the exclusive rights holder for MotoGP, with a commitment to providing live or same-day coverage of every round.

Perhaps most importantly given the changing media landscape of recent years, it will also bring MotoGP onto one of the market’s major streaming platforms as it will appear on Disney+.

The news should come as welcome relief to US fans after quite a bit of uncertainty in recent years over where exactly to watch MotoGP.

Prior to 2020, the championship had a deal with BeIN Sports in which its team attended multiple races in person, before a move to NBC for four years.

But while that deal was notable for being with a major network, it meant MotoGP coverage jumping around between channels, with many races not airing live. A new deal for 2024 with TNT Sports (announced only hours before the start of the season) didn’t prove to be substantially different.

MotoGP moved to Fox in 2025, again announced only hours before the opening session of the first weekend, and again coverage moved around between channels, with this year’s American Grand Prix at Austin airing live on Fox Business.

With that in mind, the new ESPN deal should come as welcome news not just to MotoGP fans but to the series’ new Liberty Media owner, by providing a valuable growth platform as it attempts to replicate its success with Formula 1 in the US market.

"This agreement with ESPN marks an important milestone in MotoGP's growth strategy across the Americas,” said MotoGP’s deputy CEO Carlos Ezpleleta.

“ESPN's position as one of the world's leading sports broadcasters, combined with its strong connection with audiences across the United States and Latin America, makes it the ideal platform for us to continue expanding MotoGP's reach and bring the sport closer to millions of people.

“This is an exciting opportunity to introduce MotoGP to new audiences while continuing to serve our passionate existing fanbase through one of the most influential sports media brands in the world."

title: Jensen Huang’s Resignation From Nvidia Could Complicate Billions in Philanthropic Giving
author: Theodore Schleifer
text:
Jensen Huang was just becoming one of America’s biggest philanthropists before his departure as the chief executive of Nvidia. With an estimated net worth of about $145 billion , he and his wife, Lori, had built one of the country’s largest foundations, with about $9 billion in assets.

But Mr. Huang said this week that he had been unfaithful to his wife, acknowledging an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence has determined was a Chinese spy. The Times then reported that he had another affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him. Nvidia said on Thursday morning that Mr. Huang was resigning from the company he had led for 33 years.

The fate of the foundation, which the couple started in 2007 and oversee together, is not clear.

Ms. Huang is the foundation’s president, and Mr. Huang is its secretary and chief financial officer, according to the most recent tax return for the charitable organization, which is called the Jen-hsun & Lori Huang Foundation. In 2024, its most recent tax year on file, the foundation’s assets nearly tripled, thanks to more than $5 billion in investment gains.

Marital issues have led to major shifts in the world of philanthropy in recent years, such as the departure by Melinda French Gates from her joint charitable entity with her ex-husband, Bill, and the elevation of MacKenzie Scott as one of America’s biggest givers following her divorce from Jeff Bezos.

The Huangs’ foundation is rather low-profile: Despite being one of America’s biggest charitable entities, it has no website or lists any public staff.

And the couple had only just begun giving. The biggest public gifts by the Huangs have gone to higher-education institutions, a relatively safe and conventional place to disburse large amounts of money. They have announced a combined $180 million or so to four schools, including a $75 million donation in July to establish an art and design college at Vanderbilt University’s planned outpost in San Francisco.

Mr. Huang has described his philanthropic giving as an investment, not charity. “I don’t give anything away,” he said in 2010 , dismissing the premise of the question. “The way I think about it is I’m investing in the next generation, to help us and to inspire us to create even better and more useful technologies.”

Their giving has also intersected with what is good for Nvidia. The Huangs’ foundation bought computing time from Coreweave, a key Nvidia partner and customer, and donated $108.3 million of it to universities and other nonprofits, according to an Nvidia corporate filing in May.

Theodore Schleifer is a Times reporter covering billionaires and their impact on the world.

title: We Were Warned of Deceptive A.I. Fakes. We Got Memes.
author: Stuart A. Thompson
text:
First came the election results, then came the meme party.

In the wake of the Democratic wave of support on Election Day, content creators used artificial intelligence to flood the internet with fake videos, depicting candidates and celebrities in various states of celebration.

One A.I.-made skit, featuring replicas of the cast from the hit TV show “The Office” showed the boss adjusting to a progressive society, wearing a Pride flag sweater and calling for an emergency Diversity Day. It received more than 16 million views in one post on X.

The video was emblematic of the kinds of A.I. fakes that have coursed through social media during the midterm season. Many of the most popular videos spreading online vied for laughs and sometimes jeers — an absurd mix of outlandish events that obviously never happened.

The results are a minor relief for researchers who monitor the spread of A.I. fakery, and also a reckoning.

Experts have warned ahead of every U.S. election since at least 2020 that A.I. replicas of real people — “deepfakes” — and other deceptive content generated by the technology could upend democracy, misleading voters about scandals that never happened or salacious fake comments.

title: The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal
text:
Jensen Huang, known for sporting a black leather jacket to shareholder events, appeared to have it all. He was courted by leaders in the US and China alike, worshipped by investors and seen as a loyal family man. But a rockstar approach to his personal life has ultimately led to his resignation.

The 63-year-old has been married since 1985, long before the foundation of Nvidia, the company that propelled him to tech stardom.

He is known as a workaholic and a demanding manager, with high standards for those who worked for him, which included his own children, promoted within the company. But he has seen his personal reputation go into freefall this week, undone by romantic entanglements that throw doubt on his focus and his judgement.

On Thursday, he resigned following back-to-back revelations of two affairs. News of the first - a relationship with a businesswoman alleged to be a Chinese spy - ricocheted around the world, raising eyebrows among investors. It was followed on Wednesday by reports that the tech boss had also had an affair with an Nvidia colleague.

His departure creates uncertainty in the global stock market, which was already knocked-off balance in recent weeks. Nvidia is a linchpin in the US's race for technology leadership with China.

Huang may not be a household name on the same level as Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg.

But his role in the tech industry, especially in relation to the explosion of artificial intelligence in the last three years, may prove more consequential. Nvidia dominates the market for the microchips that are used to power the new technology.

The company, which is still valued at nearly $4n (£3.02tn) despite recent events, is at the centre of the AI race between the US and China, the world's tech and economic powerhouses.

Huang enjoyed access to the seats of political power on an unrivalled scale, being courted by both US President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping.

His remarkable rise to the top of his profession has led to him being dubbed the "Taylor Swift of tech" and seen him amass an estimated fortune of $145bn, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

Despite always donning his trademark all-black outfits and taking a playful approach to investor presentations, Huang has worked for years to present himself as a family man, someone who exemplified the American Dream.

Born in Taiwan in 1963, Huang and his family moved to the west coast of the US when he was nine years old. He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a Master's degree in the same field from Stanford University.

It was at college where he met his wife, Lori Mills. The pair were lab partners and married in 1985, eight years before Huang founded Nvidia.

They have two children, Madison and Spencer, who now both work in senior roles at Nvidia.

The company became a key provider of the computer chips and circuits used for gaming before it expanded in a new direction. It now creates the key processing chips used to power the growing AI technology.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after tech giant rocked by second affair allegation

Who could replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia's chief executive?

Huang has hailed AI as a "new industrial revolution" that is on par with the advent of electricity. Nvidia is the world's second most valuable company and its customers include the biggest firms on the planet, Google, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, SpaceX, Tesla, OpenAI and Anthropic, all spending big on its products.

So it is no surprise that at a recent AI summit at the White House, Huang was picked out from a group of 42 to flank the president, alongside Elon Musk, both men with whom Trump has famously close relationships.

"Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine, a biography on Jensen Huang, told the BBC, referring to the late boss of Apple. He added that Huang was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today.

He described him as a "demanding" boss, who "really pushes his people to the limit".

But while the former Nvidia CEO is "very brilliant" and a "world-class computer scientist", there's also "a level of arrogance" and "a level of self-deception as well", he said.

Huang had gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man, he added, something that was "very important to him".

"He praises his wife, he talks about her in very glowing ways," Witt added. "The fallout of this would be bad for anyone's family. But for someone who has gone to such great lengths to cultivate an image of being a family guy and who keeps his children very close, it is very bad."

First reports emerged on 29 October in the New York Times that Huang had conducted a relationship with Alice Huang, no relation. US officials allege the businesswoman associated with Singapore-based firm Megaspeed is a Chinese intelligence asset.

After the revelations of the first affair, Huang admitted to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting their family.

Trump, as well as other leaders in the AI tech industry, initially backed Huang to continue in his role at Nvidia. The president described him as "honourable".

But the reporting of a second affair, with Kimberly Powell, vice president of healthcare who has worked at Nvidia for 18 years, prompted a board meeting, followed by the announcement Huang was stepping down.

In the aftermath of that news Trump said Huang had done "a fantastic job" and proposed Tim Cook of Apple as a suitable replacement at the head of Nvidia.

title: Carrick sacked by Manchester United with team in Premier League relegation zone – as it happened
author: John Brewin; Luke McLaughlin and John Ashdown
text:
The Manchester United Supporters’ Trust (MUST) earlier issued a statement following Carrick’s dismissal pinning the blame for poor results firmly on the ownership. In full below:

Michael Carrick’s departure marks another depressing moment for Manchester United. We thank him for his service and for restoring hope during the second half of last season. His standing among supporters remains undiminished.

The reason Manchester United fans have continued to support Michael Carrick in recent weeks is that they know that responsibility for United’s problems do not primarily rest with him or indeed his predecessors as manager.

The Glazers’ debt-funded takeover continues to burden the club. When INEOS came in they promised sporting excellence, but yet with repeated changes in football leadership we have seen anything but.

It is time for the owners to explain themselves and show some accountability.

But the discontent at United is not just about matters on the pitch. Far from it.

Aggressive ticketing policies have further damaged relations with supporters. Treating loyal fans principally as a source of revenue undermines their identity and the bond with the team that sustains support through difficult times. Supporters are being asked to pay the price for the owners’ mismanagement as well as their stadium ambitions through higher charges and diminished rights.

The earlier Stretford End banner declaring “The way you treat us is a disgrace” was a warning. The unprecedented scale of the booing at Old Trafford, alongside public criticism from senior players in recent weeks, now points to a deeper deterioration. These are signs of a club becoming more divided, with the bond between supporters, players and those running Manchester United under increasing strain.

MUST warned publicly in January 2025 that alienating supporters risked a downward spiral of worsening atmosphere, performances and financial outcomes. Our subsequent Telegraph article urged Sir Jim Ratcliffe to break that “doom loop” by bringing supporters with him. Those warnings remain painfully relevant.

The owners must allow senior club management to change direction: show accountability, rebuild trust, listen to supporters and recognise that their loyalty is fundamental to football success. Another change of head coach cannot repair what the ownership continues to undermine.

title: Fitness, Fernandes and a back four: how next head coach can reignite Manchester United | Will Unwin
author: Will Unwin
text:
Michael Carrick’s replacement must find solutions on the pitch and pressure the hierarchy to accept a share of blame

One of the final images of Michael Carrick’s time in charge will be of him standing in the rain on the Old Trafford touchline watching his side succumb to Bournemouth , while his sullen captain sat unused on the bench. Bruno Fernandes was dropped after calling out his head coach’s tactics, although Carrick said it was for football reasons. It was the second combustible television interview in as many Champions League games after Lisandro Martínez pointed the finger at the director of football, Jason Wilcox, for failing to provide a squad suitable for fighting on all fronts.

Fernandes was soon back in the fold, and Martínez apologised for his outburst , but it is clear internal discipline is an issue and will be central to getting the team back on track. United will always draw more attention than almost any other club in the world and creating a circus around a failing team merely complicates matters when there are already enough problems to sort out on the pitch. The players need to harness their anger to ensure they create headlines for performances, not interviews.

One player Jason Wilcox could claim as a recruitment success was Senne Lammens but the goalkeeper’s form has joined that of his teammates in the gutter. The Belgian endured a horror show for Bournemouth’s third goal when he rushed out of his area, and he made two errors in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa . Leny Yoro was another to make a terrible mistake against Bournemouth, while Diogo Dalot’s efforts as a makeshift left-back can be categorised as somewhere between woeful and inept. No team in Europe’s top five leagues have conceded more than United’s 30 in all competitions, which is clearly a worry.

Morale is at rock bottom but the chopping and changing in defence is creating more uncertainty. The new head coach should pick a back four and stick with it where possible. If Harry Maguire’s experience is deemed mandatory, he needs pace around him to make up for what he lacks. Luke Shaw’s absence has created a left-back tombola as Dalot, Ayden Heaven and Noussair Mazraoui have been placed there.

Benjamin Sesko’s injury has cost United a No 9 for most of the season and Joshua Zirkzee has rarely been trusted in the role. Matheus Cunha gave it a go as a false 9 and Bryan Mbeumo was tried as a more traditional centre-forward but without much success either. Cunha has become more productive in a deeper role behind the striker, cutting in from the left as he did at Wolves, but United require someone to be a classic No 9, someone who can occupy defenders and be serviced by deliveries from wide. Zirkzee, for his faults, has been a presence when used in recent weeks and scored against Aston Villa. If a new coach can rebuild his confidence, the Dutchman could provide a short-term solution. Alternatively, greater demands should be made of Marcus Rashford to play through the middle.

A mix-and-match of expletives were aimed at those above Carrick at recent home games. Wilcox has taken most of the individual criticism, but the ownership were told in no uncertain terms to sell up. The Glazers have been instrumental in driving the club downwards in recent years and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s investment and involvement in football operations have yielded little success.

Carrick was the face of the operation, as the new head coach will be, and he needs to put pressure on someone at the top to speak to the media to explain why the club is in such a mess because it is unfair to expect the coach to do so. United fans know the person in the dugout cannot take all the blame and someone else has to be publicly accountable.

Three central midfielders and a backup goalkeeper did not make for an inspiring summer when everyone knew United’s squad required improvement in numerous positions. Andrey Santos, Carlos Baleba and Youri Tielemans started together against Bournemouth and offered no evidence for why so much was spent on them.

Whoever comes in needs to be clear about what is required, whether in the winter or summer windows, because the deficiencies in the squad mean United cannot compete on all fronts and are struggling to cope with the rigours of the Premier League. A new left-back and striker are a given, but there is plenty more work to be done.

Outrunning the opposition does not guarantee success but United have looked pedestrian on far too many occasions this season. This could explain the number of slow starts to games in recent times: in the Champions League against Atlético Madrid and Como they conceded in the first and second minute respectively, and were two down at home to Roma after 17 minutes last week. Worse still, Aston Villa, aided by errors, were two goals ahead within four minutes at Old Trafford, giving United a monumental task to turn things around. The players deserve credit for finding some fight to do so but need to make life easier for themselves because it does not take a genius to work out starting with a deficit is ill-advised. They will face a fiery atmosphere at Anfield, and that will be a fine place to show a shift in dynamic.

title: Van Rysel Drops Weight and Adds Aero to the New RCR-R Lineup
author: Josh Ross
text:
Today Van Rysel is launching a new version of the RCR-R and RCR-R PRO all-around race bikes. This is a continuation of the work that started when Van Rysel, Decathlon’s in-house performance cycling brand, sprang to life in Lille, France, in 2019. The brand then really catapulted into the global spotlight when it took over as the bike sponsor for the Decathlon CMA CGM WorldTour team in 2024.

As part of that sponsorship, Van Rysel splits its lineup between the RCR-F dedicated aero platform and the RCR as a lightweight generalist. Today’s launch is an attempt to bring what Van Rysel learned from the dedicated aero platform into the generalist racing chassis while dropping weight.

While Van Rysel is part of the larger Decathlon organization, the team has historically operated like a much more nimble brand. Part of that agility is evident in the relatively short development cycle we are seeing here. According to the brand, this new platform is the result of a mere two-and-a-half-year turnaround, driven heavily by direct feedback from the Decathlon CMA CGM team.

To land on the final shape, Van Rysel worked through a claimed 13 CFD iterations, five wind-tunnel prototypes, and seven different carbon layups. The stated goal was to find the sweet spot between the aerodynamics of the dedicated RCR-F PRO and the feel of a lightweight climbing bike. To pull that off, the company essentially tried to split the difference across the chassis. By marrying a rigid front end for aerodynamic power transfer with a rear triangle that allows for controlled flex, Van Rysel claims the design mimics the traction and high-speed descending stability of a dedicated climber without sacrificing the speed of an aero rig.

Van Rysel also worked aerodynamic bottles and cages into the overall design. This approach is not unlike what we have seen from Trek and Enve, and the reasoning is obvious: it provides free aero gains with virtually no downside, provided it is executed well. Unfortunately, we won’t know how well it works right away. The images shared only show standard bottles, and Van Rysel notes that “the aero bottles will be released separately from the bikes, with further details to follow.” Despite the delay, the brand claims that in testing featuring turbulence and pedaling legs, the proprietary bottle setup saves up to 6.3 watts at 45 km/h (28 mph) over the previous generation.

Ultimately, both the PRO and the standard model share the exact same silhouette and geometry. They differ only in their carbon fiber layups and component build options, though both frames reportedly utilize the identical 360-gram fork.

At the top of the hierarchy sits the RCR-R PRO. To drop the weight on this tier, Van Rysel relies on a specific blend of super-high-modulus and high-modulus carbon fiber. According to the brand, this layup brings a size medium frame down to 705 grams, making it the lightest chassis the company has ever produced. On the scale, that translates to a claimed complete bike weight of 6.6 kg (14.5 lbs) for the flagship SRAM RED AXS build. For component options, the PRO tier is offered in four configurations: Shimano Dura-Ace Di2, Shimano Ultegra Di2, SRAM RED AXS, and SRAM Force AXS.

Sitting below the flagship model is the standard RCR-R, aimed at riders wanting the new chassis at a more accessible price point. While it uses the same aerodynamic mold as the PRO, Van Rysel relies on a standard high-modulus carbon layup for this tier. That shift in material adds a bit of mass, pushing the claimed frame weight up to 883 grams. On the complete bike side, the Ultegra Di2 build is the lightest configuration offered, tipping the scales at a claimed 7.4 kg (16.3 lbs). To keep costs down, the brand is speccing this frame exclusively with mid-to-upper-tier electronic groupsets, giving buyers the choice of Shimano 105 Di2 or Ultegra Di2, as well as SRAM Rival AXS or Force AXS.

While Van Rysel pulled the cover off the new bikes today at Rouleur Live in London, they won’t be hitting showroom floors immediately. Commercial availability is slated to open after the new year on January 5, 2027. When they do go on sale, European pricing will range from €3,299 up to €8,499 depending on the chosen frame tier and component build. For more details on the new lineup, visit the Van Rysel website .

title: Van Rysel announces the new RCR-R Pro bike featuring its lightest ever frame
author: thomas.wieckowski@futurenet.com (Tom Wieckowski)
text:
Van Rysel has announced two new additions to its range today in the form of new RCR-R Pro and RCR-R models.

The RCR-R Pro is an existing model in the brand's range, but this updated version offers the same frame design in two carbon fibre layup specs and build ranges.

If this news jogs your memory to chatter about Van Rysel prototypes from the summer, you would be right. We first spotted a prototype being raced by Paul Seixas at the Tour Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes back in June.

We also got another good luck at said bike at the Tour de France in July, before Seixas took a thunderous solo win on it at Il Lombardia later in the year.

The time is now seemingly right to unveil the bike officially, coinciding with the bike going on show at Rouleur Live, which takes place in London this weekend.

All bikes will be available to buy from the 5th of January 2027, and Van Rysel says it will be providing a white paper between now and then with more technical details on the bike; here's what we have so far.

Van Rysel has an aero bike in the form of the RCR-F Pro and categorises the RCR-R Pro as a lightweight aerodynamic road bike. The brand says it's been developed to be fast across a range of terrains.

Development has taken place over a span of two and a half years with feedback from the Decathlon CMA CGM team, and as is often the case, the brand says that CFD (computational fluid dynamics), wind tunnel testing, and pro feedback have gone into the development.

Both bike models share the same frame design, but vary in their weights and carbon layups.

The RCR-R Pro uses a mix of super high modulus and high modulus carbon fibre. It weighs a claimed 705 grams for a size medium and is, according to the brand, Van Rysel's lightest ever frame.

The RCR-R frame uses high-modulus carbon and weighs in at a claimed 883 grams for a size medium. The frames both use the same 360-gram fork.

As is the case with most bikes, a blend of features has been sought; Van Rysel says it has looked to combine front-end stiffness with rear-end flex.

Van Rysel tested 13 CFD prototypes, five wind tunnel prototypes and seven frame lay ups before arriving at the bike's final form.

A new aerodynamic water bottle and cage has also been developed, the aero bottles will be released seperately from the bike, but the brand is claiming up to a 6.3 watt saving at 45km/h compared to the previous generation in testing with 'turning legs and turbulence.'

Some WorldTour teams have aero bottles and cages at their disposal but are limited by sponsorship agreements, it remains to be seen whether the team will race with the new components.

Van Rysel says Decathlon CMA CGM riders tested the bike in training and competition this year, with at least Paul Seixas, Nicolas Prodhomme and Matthew Riccitello testing RCR-R PRO prototypes, with Seixas himself saying:

"The bike is lighter, more aerodynamic and, above all, more stable on descents. When you’re travelling at over 100 km/h, confidence in your kit is paramount.

"I clocked up the kilometres in training and worked closely with the Van Rysel engineers to fine-tune the final settings before switching to race mode for the second half of the season. Winning a Monument on this bike is the ultimate validation."

We got a look at one of Seixas' prototypes before the Tour de France kicked off in Barcelona earlier in the year. It was a good chance to take a look at the bike's curved seat tube and profiled stem cover and spacers.

The frame design looks largely the same, but Seixas appeared to ride a raw, unpainted version, which must have saved some extra weight over a painted model.

RCR-R Pro bikes will be available in Shimano Dura-Ace Di2 and Ultegra Di2 builds, as well as SRAM Red and Force.

Complete weights for a medium are a claimed 6.6kg for a SRAM Red build, 6.8kg for a Dura-Ace, and 7.1kg for both Ultegra and Force options.

RCR-R builds will be available in SRAM Force and Rival, as well as Shimano Ultegra and 105 Di2.

Complete weights for a medium are claimed at 7.4 kg for a Shimano Ultegra build, 7.5kg for Force, 7.8kg for 105 and 7.9kg for Rival.

Bikes will range from €3,299 to €8,499, but we don't have any model-specific pricing right now.

title: Mike Brown is sticking with Mikal Bridges. For now.
author: Russell Richardson
text:
In last night’s loss to the Cavaliers, Mikal Bridges played 17 minutes, took three shots, and finished with two points, two rebounds, and an assist. This was another disappointing performance in a season when we expected the wing to make his first All-Star appearance.

At his presser after the game, coach Mike Brown said: “Mikal is a starter, and so it’s not a question of that. He’s like a lot of players. They’ve had their good moments and their not-so-good moments. And Mikal has a proven track record of playing at a pretty high level as a starter in this league. So, for me to make a quote-unquote panic decision and change it right now, we’re ten games in, or whatever we are, I’m not feeling it.”

And in the locker room, Jalen Brunson defended his teammate. “The people in this room have his back night in & night out. We see the work he puts into his game, […] Regardless of what the noise is on the outside, that’s our brother.”

Bridges is an iron man. Between college ball and the pros, he hasn’t missed a game. He’s also one of Jalen Brunson’s closest friends on the team, and as Villanova teammates they won two national titles together. Kal’s mantle is full of pre-pro awards, and he was named to the NBA All-Defensive First Team in 2022. Bridges is a world champion. With a lithe, long body, he’s a tremendous cutter, plays a terrific midrange game, and guards multiple positions well. He’s a career 48% / 37% / 84% shooter, averaging over 14 points and 1.2 steals per game. Maybe not Hall-of-Fame, but definitely Hall-of-Pretty-Good.

In 2024, Brooklyn traded him to New York for a boatload of picks. In just over two seasons at his current home, he’s averaged more than 15 points per game and has been a fixture of the starting lineup.

He’s also been consistently inconsistent. There were times last season when we thought it might be time to sacrifice the games-played streak for a little RnR. After the first five games of the playoffs, we were ready to leave him behind in Atlanta. Then he went on an incredible run, and aside from faltering somewhat against the Spurs, he was essential to New York bringing home a championship. As we know, winning heals a lot of wounds. Those same fans who complained about the overpay soon took up a delirious chant about defiling those picks.

You cannot deny the man’s achievements—nor that he’s stunk so far this season. After a summer of celebration, the 30-year-old has started the current campaign with some of the worst play of his career. Eleven games in, his stats are 5.9 PPG, 33% FG, and 27% 3PT. These Knicks are notoriously late starters, often not hitting their stride until late in the first or even second quarter. Or the fourth. Cap even joked about this in his SNL appearance. But this time, Mikal has no stride to hit. Lately, he has watched the fourth quarter action from the bench (very expensive seats, indeed).

Mike Brown is a supreme diplomat, saying all the right things at all times. Yet, Mikal is a starter because the coach chooses to start him. That’s the coach’s prerogative. The skipper could field someone else as the starting shooting guard—say Landry Shamet, who’s proven himself more than worthy. Why hasn’t he?

First, there’s a chemistry to the team that Mike Brown handles like plutonium. To disrupt the starting five by separating Kal from his ‘Nova brethren might yield positive results on the court, but could foment discord behind the scenes. A demotion could also further erode Bridges’ confidence, which would be bad for their long-term plans. Unless he’s shipped off before the midseason trade deadline (more musings on that below), the Knicks will need Bridges in shape physically and mentally for a deep postseason run.

Further, there’s the potential loss of a reliable sparkplug off the bench. For a while now, Shamet’s been the most consistent in that role. McBride and Clarkson have certainly had their moments, too, but when Mike needs a sub AND a bucket AND defense, ShamWow has become his security blanket. When the score is close, Landry’s steady contribution makes it difficult to justify giving those two-guard minutes to Bridges in the final frame.

Here’s Brown again, from his postgame. “Yeah, part of it is we got two guys that are playing really well in Landry and Deuce, and so it’s hard. [… They] have been a big part of what we’ve done defensively. If they’re playing at a high level, I got to keep trying to find ways to get those guys on the floor.”

As Brown alluded, the Knicks have more guards than they need. Conversely, they remain light at the center position. They have Karl-Anthony Towns playing a career year, Andre Drummond backing him up with great rebounds and questionable shots, and . . . James Wiseman? Sometimes? Leon Rose & Co. are aware of this. They also know that in a trade for a big man of talent, they will need both a desirable player to offer and one whose salary helps to offset what’s incoming.

Obviously, Bridges is a nice guy. He’s not so diabolical as to throw his season to insulate himself from being traded. His sub-standard play does complicate trade opportunities, however. Another club that’s willing to part with a talented center will want to take on a positive, productive player, not a distressed asset with a lot of basketball miles on his wheels.

There’s also a not insignificant chance that the front office is totally cool with what they have and are unwilling to make a panic move either. After all, the team that won the Finals did so with Karl-Anthony Towns, occasional Mitchell Robinson, and a sprinkling of Ariel Hukporti. If Brown can coach Wiseman up to Huk-level participation, then what’s the difference, really?

When asked about his play earlier in this short season, Bridges said, “Obviously we should be better than we are, me personally,” he said. “But it takes time and just not skipping steps.”

He doesn’t sound panicked. Neither does Mike after 11 games. Nor Jalen, Leon, or the rest of the team. What about 15 games? 20? Can we run screaming down the street on December 1st? Ideally, Bridges gets right in Friday’s game against Indy, kills the conversation for the rest of the season, and we all look back and laugh. If this continues to be an issue, though, we’re very interested to see Mike’s next move.

title: Hearing set for Audi Tsunoda appeal
author: Jon Noble
text:
The FIA has announced that Audi’s appeal against Yuki Tsunoda not getting a penalty at Formula 1’s Italian Grand Prix will be heard on November 25.

Audi complained after the Monza race for what it felt was an incorrect application of the rules against Tsunoda for an alleged grid infringement at the restart.

Tsunoda had been due to line up 14th but, after mistakenly initially heading towards the 15th-place grid slot, he veered at the last-minute to the right-hand side.

While he was able to come to a stop within his intended grid slot, so therefore was not out of position over the front, his Racing Bulls car had ended up at an angle.

That was enough for race director Rui Marques to decide to go for another formation lap because, according to a later stewards' document, "he stated he was not comfortable starting the race with the car in that position".

Tsunoda’s actions had triggered an FIA stewards’ investigation because drivers that cause an extra formation lap are deemed to be in breach of the rules.

Any driver who causes an additional formation lap but is able to start that lap is required to "enter the pitlane at the end of the lap and must start the [session] from the end of the pitlane".

With Tsunoda not serving that, F1's sporting regulations state that any unserved stop-and-go penalty is converted to a 30-second post-race time penalty.

Racing Bulls argued, however, that Tsunoda had not the extra formation lap - as he was still within his grid box and was not impacting any other drivers.

The stewards accepted that position and felt that Tsunoda himself had not been the “cause” of the extra formation lap – which was instead down to Marques’ own choice.

Audi complained, though, as it felt that Tsunoda had indeed been the catalyst for the extra formation lap.

It said in a short statement after Monza that it had "raised a concern regarding the application of Article B5.9.4".

Audi would stand to benefit were Tsunoda to be penalised, because a 30-second sanction would drop him to 15th - with Gabriel Bortoleto being promoted to 10th.

The matter will now be heard at the FIA’s International Court of Appeal in Paris on November 25. The hearing will take place behind closed doors at the request of the FIA, so no public nor media will be allowed to attend.

title: Gaia Realini heads for 'new adventure' with Picnic-PostNL, but can climber rejuvenate her career? – Analysis
author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
text:
Gaia Realini has announced that she's departing Lidl-Trek for a move to Picnic-PostNL next season.

The Italian had spent the past four seasons with Lidl-Trek, with both her and the German team agreeing to end her contract a year early this winter. Now, she's on the move to Dutch squad Picnic-PostNL , she announced in an Instagram post.

"After four years with Lidl-Trek, it's time to start a new chapter. Thank you for all the experiences and moments we shared," Realini wrote.

"I'm happy to announce that I will join Picnic-PostNL for next season, a team that has believed in me from the very beginning and our first conversations.

"New colours, new goals, and plenty of motivation to give my best. Ready for this new adventure!"

After joining Lidl-Trek from Italian squad Isolmant-Premac-Vittoria, Realini had impressed during her first two seasons with the team. She emerged as a top climber, taking podium finishes at the UAE Tour, La Flèche Wallonne, La Vuelta Femenina, and Giro d'Italia in 2023.

Meanwhile, a fifth place at the Tour de France Femmes was her highlight of 2024. She hasn't hit those heights in the past two seasons, however, after suffering a fractured elbow in early 2025.

Her top stage race result of the past two seasons came this September with a 10th-place finish at the Faun Tour Femmes.

Realini is the sixth rider to leave Lidl-Trek for 2027, joining cyclo-cross world champion Lucinda Brand and under-23 world time trial champion Felicity Wilson-Haffenden among notable names on the outgoing list as former Tour de France Femmes champion Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney heads their incoming transfers.

She is, to date, the only confirmed addition for Picnic-PostNL this off-season, while Pfeiffer Georgi, Megan Arens, Rachele Barbieri, and Elise Uijen are on the way out.

title: From washing dishes at Denny’s to rockstar of AI: the rise and fall of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang
author: Dan Milmo Global technology editor
text:
Technical expertise and an ability to engage gave the chipmaker’s co-founder, who has now resigned, the edge with customers and investors

Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after alleged affairs

Jensen Huang wasn’t always in his trademark leather jacket. When the multibillionaire, now former Nvidia chief executive was a teenager in the US, his first job was waiting tables and washing dishes at a branch of Denny’s.

“It teaches you humility, it teaches you hard work, it teaches you hospitality,” he said in 2023 of his time at the diner chain.

Decades later, having become one of the richest people on the planet, Huang put on a Denny’s apron in tribute to his former employer at an Nvidia event in 2025.

By this point Huang had become a rockstar of the artificial intelligence boom – befitting his signature item of clothing – feted around the world by investors, fellow tech executives and politicians.

The company that Huang co-founded makes the computer chips that are integral to the development and operation of AI systems such as ChatGPT.

Demand for Nvidia’s products has surged as hundreds of billions of dollars have been poured into a technology that, according to its many promotors, will transform the global economy. The crude analogy is that Huang and Nvidia have become the main purveyors of shovels in the AI gold rush.

In technical jargon, its AI chips are known as graphics processor units (GPUs), which were originally designed to handle the graphics for video games. But it turned out that a GPU’s ability to carry out masses of technical calculations simultaneously and quickly is very handy for developing and operating AI systems, which have a voracious appetite for data crunching.

Nvidia is also very good at creating networks of its chips, which produces the computing power artificial intelligence needs, and provides the CUDA software that helps the company’s GPUs perform so well for AI customers.

Jen-Hsun Huang, 63, was born in Taiwan to a chemical engineer father and a schoolteacher mother. Decades later, the island would become the centre of chip manufacturing and the foundry for Nvidia’s highly advanced chips.

But his life was largely lived outside Taiwan. After a spell living in Thailand, Huang moved to the US when he was 10 – he is a joint citizen of Taiwan and the US – and has said he is “always an immigrant”.

Accidentally enrolled by his uncle into a juvenile reform school in Kentucky, he anglicised his name and showed educational flair. Huang went to high school in Oregon and in 1984 he graduated with a degree in electrical engineering from Oregon State University, where he met his future wife, Lori, with whom he had a son and a daughter, both now Nvidia employees.

He then completed a master’s degree in the same subject at Stanford University – in the heart of Silicon Valley – in 1992. A year later he founded Nvidia with fellow engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, during a meeting in a booth at Denny’s. The name is a riff on the Latin term for envy, invidia , an emotion that the company wanted its rivals to feel.

Huang’s technical expertise also gave him an edge with customers and investors, according to The Nvidia Way, a biography of the company and its co-founder by Tae Kim.

The book quotes Tench Coxe, an Nvidia board member and early investor, who said Huang stood out.

“When you meet Jensen Huang, even with dozens of other graphics companies, you realise this is a guy you want to do business with,” said Tench. “What made him great is he is an engineer and he is a computer scientist.”

Nvidia started out making graphics chips for personal computers. It released what is widely regarded as the world’s first GPU, the GeForce 256, in 1999 and as the technology became more and more powerful academic researchers realised it could accelerate AI development. Nvidia GPUs were used to create AlexNet, the neural network developed by Alex Krizhevsky, the OpenAI-co-founder Ilya Sutskever and the Nobel prize winner Geoffrey Hinton at the University of Toronto in 2012 – and a key moment in the history of modern AI.

Six months after the launch of ChatGPT, Nvidia’s valuation reached $1tn (£756bn) in May 2023 and kept growing, hitting $5tn on October last year – the first ever company to reach such a milestone . However, it has fallen to about $4tn this week after allegations that Huang had conducted affairs with a Chinese spy and an Nvidia executive, leading to his resignation on Thursday.

Huang’s 3.6% stake in Nvidia has given him considerable wealth. His fortune is valued at $145bn, according to Bloomberg, the 13th highest in the world.

The importance of Nvidia’s products to the AI revolution have made Huang rich, powerful and famous. He is often seen at tech conferences or in the presence of global leaders, including Donald Trump with whom he has developed a rapport. Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, another mighty Silicon Valley founder, has described Huang as “Taylor Swift, but for tech”.

One UK tech industry insider who has met Huang at various tech and government events describes the Nvidia CEO as having an “ability to engage” that marked him out from other executives in his peer group.

“He’s like a good politician,” said the source. “I think the sector has lost one of its best communicators.”

The source added that Huang had no problem getting access to the upper echelons of governments. “Everyone wanted to meet him.”

However, Huang’s undoubted drive and charisma had a flipside, according to Stephen Witt, a journalist who interviewed the executive as part of his award-winning book about Huang and his company, The Thinking Games. In his final chat with a “visibly exhausted” Huang in 2024, Witt describes the interviewee’s voice “crescendoing with anger” as he mulls a question about what new jobs will be created by AI.…

title: How Pochettino came on Man Utd's radar - and what Carrick was told when
text:
Michael Carrick must have known what was coming.

Not just because reports of his imminent dismissal were widespread - followed by information about who would be replacing him as Manchester United boss.

But because, effectively, he and his representatives were given heavy enough indications of what was to follow.

On Monday, according to well-placed sources, Carrick's agent was contacted by chief executive Omar Berrada to be told he and director of football Jason Wilcox would be heading to Monaco for a planned meeting with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe that would include a discussion about the head coach's future.

A day later, it is believed Wilcox had a similar conversation with Carrick.

It is understood that on both occasions it was communicated that a recommendation regarding Carrick's future at the club would be made.

What is not clear is whether Carrick and his representatives knew that recommendation was to relieve him of his duties.

By that point, BBC Sport has been told United were aware of a $10m (£7m) release clause in Mauricio Pochettino's contract with the United States national team. One source even indicated it was representatives of the Argentine who told the Premier League side.

There is some regret behind the scenes at United that machinations leading to Carrick's departure on Thursday were played out so publicly.

But with football clubs the size of United, keeping such developments completely private is extremely difficult - and there is a feeling they were as transparent with Carrick as they could be.

Following heavy defeats by Como and Bournemouth , United placed huge importance on the following three games - against Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa.

It is understood United's leadership team were clear with Carrick that results and performances needed to improve. A defeat, a victory and draw weren't enough to save him.

There is a feeling that during that three-game period, there was not enough progress, particularly in terms of team structure - underlined by the fact they conceded eight goals.

Pochettino finalising Man Utd deal after Carrick sacking

The chaos that took Carrick from two-year deal to sacked within 15 games

Carrick has conducted himself with great dignity during the turmoil of the past few days and he leaves the club - certainly in the eyes of supporters - with his standing as a United great intact.

When United first appointed Carrick - initially on an interim basis following the sacking of Ruben Amorim in January - he had a positive impact on the squad, and subsequently results.

United liked his positive messaging to the players and media. They felt Carrick brought calm to rocky waters and protected his players at every opportunity - a contrast from at least the closing stages of Amorim's tenure.

On the pitch, the United hierarchy felt Carrick's style of play allowed the forward players more freedom, and they won 12 of their last 17 matches of the season.

While United considered other managerial options in the summer, there was ultimately a sense Carrick had earned a shot at the job on a permanent basis.

The 45-year-old signed a two-year deal, though it is understood United contractually protected themselves in the event of an early termination.

Part of the thought process was to provide the players with some managerial stability given the increased turnover of head coaches in recent years.

Yet the season started poorly with defeat at newly promoted Hull City - and has only spiralled downward since.

United are third bottom of the Premier League and 17th in the Champions League table.

Since Monday, talks have been ongoing with Pochettino.

On Wednesday, Berrada contacted the US Soccer Federation to confirm the existence of the release clause and their intention to activate it.

It is understood the news did not come as a surprise to those across the Atlantic.

Pochettino had been clear with his employers about the discussions with United and - most pertinently - his intention to return to the Premier League.

While United want Pochettino in situ as soon as possible, they are respectful of the fact the USA have two fixtures against Haiti to play - the second of which is on 18 November.

If Pochettino takes charge of the second game, it is understood he will be in place at United's Carrington headquarters on 19 November - four days before they face Liverpool.

title: Lindblad and Lawson to continue at Racing Bulls
text:
Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson will continue as the drivers for Red Bull's second team Racing Bulls in 2027.

Red Bull had been deciding whether to promote Bulgarian Formula 2 front-runner Nikola Tsolov in place of Lawson but have decided to spend a second season assessing their current line-up

Tsolov will be the reserve driver for both teams next season.

Team principal Alan Permane said: "I have no doubt that this is the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition.

"Both have demonstrated their ability and potential throughout the season, and we've seen the progress they've made, both individually and as a pairing."

The decision to retain both marks a break from the previous Red Bull philosophy of fast-tracking drivers through the programme.

Chequered Flag Extra: The Making of Kimi Antonelli

Racing Bulls essentially exists to find potential drivers for the main Red Bull team, so the company has tended to jettison drivers who have been given a chance and not succeeded.

That's why Lawson, 24, was considered vulnerable. He was promoted to Red Bull alongside Max Verstappen for the 2025 season only to be demoted after just two races in which he had struggled.

The New Zealander has since sought to rebuild his career and was much more convincing when he was re-promoted to Red Bull for the Dutch, Italian and Spanish Grands Prix this year while regular driver Isack Hadjar was recovering from a broken wrist.

Keeping Lawson on board for 2027 gives Red Bull a known-quality benchmark with which to continue their assessment of Lindblad, who made his debut this season.

The 19-year-old Briton has excelled at times in his rookie year but on average has been a little behind Lawson, who has out-qualified him 13 times to nine and has scored more than twice as many points.

Lawson said: "We've had a brilliant season together and the team has worked very hard to produce a fast car, which I've loved driving.

"It feels great to be part of a historic season for the team as we continue our fight for fifth place in the constructors' championship.

"I'm looking forward to carrying this moment forward with Arvid through to 2027; we're building something super positive and I'm excited by what we can achieve together."

Lindblad added: "It's been a truly special year, full of new experiences and learnings since the very first pre-season test. I'd like to thank everyone for their trust and support.

"I can't wait to get started next year, building on everything I've learned during my rookie season."

The news release announcing the pairing made no mention of Tsolov, who is expected to be retained by Red Bull in some form of reserve role in which he gains experience through work in the simulator and with testing previous cars.

title: Yankees Birthday of the Day: Carl Mays
author: Andrew Mearns
text:
Carl Mays probably would’ve enjoyed one single entry in the annals of baseball lore that doesn’t mention the most regrettable of the thousands of pitches that he threw across a 15-year career that saw him capture four World Series titles. Alas, even on his 135th birthday, we cannot grant that wish. No matter how great he was on the mound, his story will always be tied to that of Cleveland shortstop Ray Chapman. That’s just how it is.

November 12, 1891 (Liberty, KY) April 4, 1971 (El Cajon, CA): 1919-23

Mays was born in Kentucky to a Methodist minister named William Mays (ah, baseball coincidences), who died when Carl was just 12 years old. The family had moved to Missouri by then, but they packed up again after William’s death, en route to Kingfisher, Oklahoma. It was a sad time for Mays’ family, but he did get the opportunity to meet his cousin, John Long. He was a catcher, and he introduced Mays to the game. Pitching to Long, Mays developed the raw skills to attract the notice of traveling teams.

At the age of 20, Mays signed with the Class D Western Tri-State League’s Boise Irrigators, who offered him $90 per month. Mays was certainly worth the deal, as he pitched to a 2.08 ERA, 0.930 WHIP, and a 22-9 record in 280.2 innings. He moved up to the Class B team in Portland and again had a fine season, though won/loss record (10-15) deceived his true performance (2.45 ERA, 1.024 WHIP in 250 innings), and it was enough to get a new contract for 1914 with the Providence Grays, a Rhode Island team owned by the Detroit Tigers.

The Boston Red Sox purchased the Grays from the Tigers during the season, and Mays attracted Boston’s interested with a fantastic season: 24-8 and a 2.57 ERA in 273.1 innings. Another young pitcher joined him down the stretch named Babe Ruth, and their pitching helped Providence win the pennant. By the beginning of next season, Mays was a major-league pitcher.

The submariner worked mostly out of the bullpen in his rookie season, appearing in 38 games but 131.2 innings overall of 90 ERA- and 69 FIP- ball. He threw hard and was not at all afraid to throw high and inside to back hitters off the plate. Even as a rookie, he made an enemy of Ty Cobb, whose own nasty attitude clashed with Mays. On one occasion, Cobb was knocked down and then dragged a bunt up the first base line, where he spiked Mays with his sharp cleats and cut his leg. Boston and Detroit fought hard for the pennant in 1915; a 100-win season was not good enough to win the title for Detroit. Boston beat the Phillies in five games for the 1915 World Series title, but while he was a champion in his first season, Mays did not appear in any of the games.

The next couple seasons saw Mays slowly transition from splitting time more evenly between the ‘pen and rotation to becoming an established rotation presence and the ace of a championship staff. Although he was a bit of a loner, there was no denying his competitiveness on the mound. The Red Sox repeated as champions in 1916, and Mays had his best year in Boston in 1917, pitching to a 1.74 ERA (69 ERA-) in 289 innings while also unsurprisingly leading the league in hit by pitches. Only two pitchers in baseball had a better ERA than Mays that year and despite the HBPs, he had a 1.052 WHIP. His pitches simply sank, and many batters could not do any better than hitting it on the ground while hoping it found a hole in the infield:

Yankees infielder Roger Peckinpaugh said Mays threw “a very ‘heavy’ ball. It sinks and when you catch it, it feels heavy enough to almost go through your glove.” Horace Ford, who batted against Mays in the National League, said that hitting Mays’s fastball “was like hitting a chuck of lead. It would go clunk and you’d beat it into the ground.”– Allan Wood, SABR

Boston finished nine games behind the White Sox for the AL pennant that year, but another fine season by Mays in 1918 brought them back on top. While his ERA and ERA- jumped a bit to 2.21 and 84, respectively, his WHIP was almost identical and he led the league in both shutouts (8) and complete games (30). Those marks were made more impressive by the fact that the season ended early after 126 games on September 2nd due to World War I. The Red Sox played the Cubs in the Fall Classic, and Mays received the ball in Game 3 with the series tied at one game apiece. He beat the Cubs 2-1, going the distance with just one walk allowed, scattering seven hits. Boston and Chicago split the next two games, so Mays got the start in Game 6 to close out the Cubbies, and he did just that by spinning a three-hitter in another 2-1 victory. Mays was the last man to throw a pitch for a championship Red Sox team in the next 86 years.

Although his teammates were not fond of Mays for his somewhat antisocial personality and irritance on the mound when they committed errors, it seemed as though Boston and Mays had a fine relationship. It all came to a sudden halt in 1919. Boston struggled to give him much run support, and Mays became highly frustrated with the offense. From a personal standpoint, his Missouri home had burned down, and he grew so annoyed with the Philadelphia fans during one series that he hurled a baseball from the dugout at a fan. Finally, in a July 13th game against the White Sox, catcher Wally Schang clocked him in the head with a throw on a stolen base by Eddie Collins.

Soon afterward, manager and future Yankees GM Ed Barrow removed him from the game, and he stormed off the field, chucking the ball against the backstop. Mays was suspended by the Red Sox and told sportswriters that he demanded a trade. Soon, owner Harry Frazee obliged, sending Mays to the Yankees on July 29th in exchange for two unremarkable pitchers and $40,000.

“Carl, this is [co-owner] Cap Huston of the Yankees. I called to find out if you would be interested in pitching for the Yankees. If you are, there’s a good chance of my swinging a deal for you tonight, but I didn’t want to get all tangled up in negotiations if you wouldn’t pitch for us.”“Well, how about the money?” “We’ll have no problems there. Just pack your bag, and by the time you get here, we’ll be ready to talk contract.”

– excerpted from Marty Appel’s “Pinstripe Empire”

AL president Ban Johnson was furious about the trade since a suspended player was dealt and essentially controlled his own fate over the authority of the Red Sox owner. The reserve clause was supposed to bind a player to his team without much control over it, but Mays worked around the system. He demanded that the trade be voided and that Mays be returned to Boston, but Yankee owners Jacob Ruppert and Cap Huston flat-out refused and told Johnson that if necessary, they would go to court to keep Mays on the Yankees. New York State Supreme Court Justice Robert F. Wagner granted a temporary injunction allowing Mays to pitch for the Yankees.

Johnson’s decision was rendered meaningless, and Mays made 13 starts for the Yankees down the stretch as the team bid to pass the infamous “Black Sox” in the AL pennant race. Although the White Sox ended up running away with the pennant as the Yankees finished in third place with an 80-59 record, it was not Mays’ fault by any means. He was outstanding, pitching to a 1.65 ERA and 51 ERA-, winning nine of his starts, completing all but one of them, and throwing a shutout as well. In just 13 starts, he was worth 2.6 rWAR and 2.2 fWAR for a rising Yankees team. They had their ace, and now they needed a hitting star. They enlisted Mays’ former rotationmate Ruth, who was a pretty fair hitter.

With Mays and Ruth in tow, the Yankees had a superb team ready for the 1920 campaign. They finished the year with a then-franchise record 95 wins and a .617 winning percentage, though they ended up behind pennant-winning Cleveland by two games. The race between the two teams was sadly marred by tragedy in a game on August 16th at the Yankees’ home, the Polo Grounds.

Mays was in the midst of another fine season, wherein he led the league with six shutouts, pitched 312 innings, and ended with a 3.06 ERA (81 ERA-). The unpopular Mays faced perhaps his polar opposite at the plate leading off the fifth inning in beloved Cleveland shortstop Ray Chapman, a perennially fantastic player who had already amassed a 28.9 fWAR career in just nine years and 1,051 games with Cleveland. He was only 29, a potential Hall of Famer in the making. Even Cobb liked him. However, Chapman had a tendency to lean over the plate, and Mays threw an inside fastball toward him to start this at-bat. What happened next was unclear: either Chapman ducked unfortunately right into the ball’s path attempting a drag bunt, or he never moved at all. Either way, it got him square in the temple with a sickeningly loud crack.

It struck Chapman so hard that the ball caromed back toward the mound, and Mays’ immediate action was to throw the ball to first base in case it hit Chapman’s bat. Chapman’s teammates helped him off the field, as he was still conscious. They brought him to St. Lawrence Hospital, where he was diagnosed with a fractured skull and died the next day, the only player to ever die as the result of a pitch in an MLB game.

“It was the most regrettable incident of my career, and I would give anything if I could undo what has happened.“– Carl Mays

The whole incident was a horrible experience for everyone involved; Mays was contrite but overall did not handle it particularly well, noting that there was scuff on the ball (which he always normally liked to do anyway), and that he didn’t expect Chapman to duck into the ball. He insisted to his dying day that he did not throw at Chapman. Regardless, the tragedy only emphasized the reason why baseball banned the spitball at the beginning of the year, with only those who already threw it allowed to use it via grandfather clause. Strangely, it still took over 35 years before players started wearing helmets in the batter’s box.

Mays became synonymous with Chapman’s death, and while he pitched another nine years in The Show, most people only remember Mays for that tragic pitch. Mays’ best season in New York actually occurred the very next year. He did what he could to put the incident behind him and paced the league with 27 wins, 49 games (38 starts), and a career-high 336.2 innings pitched. He was brilliant in a 4.5-fWAR campaign, and the Bombers outlasted Cleveland to win their first pennant in franchise history. Mays completed nine of his ten starts down the stretch and even tossed in a relief appearance; the Yankees won all but one of those games.

In the first game of the unusual best-of-nine, all-Polo Grounds World Series against John McGraw’s Giants, Mays put the Yankees ahead with a dominant five-hit shutout. He didn’t walk anyone, and only two batters made it past first base. The teams split the next two games, and Mays had the chance to give the Yankees a 3-1 series lead in Game 4, but Phil Douglas outpitched him. Mays held a slim 1-0 lead into the top of the eighth, but an Irish Meusel triple, singles by Johnny Rawlings and Fred Snyder, and a two-run double by George Burns gave the Giants three runs. The Yankees lost 4-2 to even the series.…

title: Matthew Richardson Allegedly Targeted Teammate With Offensive Images in Track Worlds Scandal
author: Jim Cotton
text:
(Photo: Dilara Irem Sancar/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Matthew Richardson was sent home from the UCI track world championships last month in disgrace after he allegedly targeted a teammate with offensive images.

That’s the new detail The Times reported Tuesday on a scandal that’s rocked the small world of track cycling.

The Times wrote that Richardson – one of the best sprinters of his era – had left a long regular trail of homophobic and discriminatory remarks about people from minority backgrounds.

One of those was made in a message that included “a deeply offensive image with reference to another Team GB rider.”

The image sparked an allegation being made against Richardson.

The complaint saw him sent home from Shanghai by British Cycling on the eve of October’s UCI track worlds.

“The Times has seen extensive evidence, dating back over a number of years, of images and messages sent by Richardson to other riders. He appears to make discriminatory remarks about people from minority backgrounds on a regular basis,” reads the report.

“The Times has seen six different messages where he appears to use the racially offensive n-word, and others where he jokes about his use of that word. He also appears to have made a number of offensive references to the Asian community and homophobic comments. Another senior source claims to have seen a separate image, again sent to riders, that references a rider from another international team and uses the n-word.”

Richardson was born in England but moved to Australia as a child.

He switched racing nationality from Australian to English in 2024.

British Cycling confirmed it opened an investigation into Richardson’s conduct after he was axed from its world championship squad.

The 27-year-old vowed he would fully co-operate in the proceedings “with contrition.”

However, according to The Times, the allegations against Richardson dated back to July – three months before the investigation was opened. Additionally, Richardson was only withdrawn 48 hours before the world championships in Shanghai last month.

These developments come at a difficult time for British Cycling.

In a separate thread, The Times reported that an independent feedback survey of the federation uncovered a drop in morale among elite riders, a lack of accountability in senior leadership, and accusations of a “toxic culture.”

Richardson’s agent has distanced himself from the rider in the wake of the allegations against the rider.

However, Richardson is still headlining the London 3-Day track cycling event this weekend. The event is not affiliated to British Cycling.

British Cycling has not provided any timelines on the conclusion of its investigation.

title: Netcompany Ineos end long-term partnership with Continental to switch to Pirelli tyres for 2027
author: thomas.wieckowski@futurenet.com (Tom Wieckowski)
text:
Netcompany Ineos will race on Pirelli tyres from 2027 onwards, bringing an end to a a long-term partnership with Continental.

Launching as Sky Procycling in 2010, the British team used a range of tyres from manufacturers like Veloflex, FMB, and Vittoria in their early years, but have consistently used Continental for more than a decade now.

However, a new three-year agreement with Pirelli was. announced on Thursday.

"Pirelli bring a huge amount of technical expertise and a real commitment to innovation, so it's exciting to have them working closely with our riders and performance team," said the team's Director of Racing, Geraint Thomas.

"It's not just about the equipment we race on, but how we can work together to keep developing, so we're really looking forward to building that relationship and seeing what we can achieve together."

Netcompany Ineos will make their racing debut on Pirelli rubber at the Santos Tour Down Under in January.

'Marginal gains' is still a phrase that's closely linked to Netcompany Ineos, and there is some mention of that philosophy in the Pirelli press release.

Pirelli says the partnership will focus on developing 'technical solutions' to the demands of WorldTour cycling. There's also a mention of 'technical assessment' being a key step in the development of the partnership.

In simple language, this could point to the team testing the Pirelli tyres against the Continental GP 5000 S TR and TT TR tyres they have been racing on until now.

Pirelli already supplies two WorldTour teams: Lidl-Trek and Alpecin-Premier Tech.

It sounds like Netcompany Ineos will primarily use the Pirelli P Zero Race SL-R tyre as well as the P Zero Race RS model.

The team also switched wheels at the start of this year, moving from Shimano Dura-Ace wheels to Scope models. Perhaps the Scope wheels and Pirelli tyre combination has proven to be faster.

We tested road tyres in our CN Labs tyre test in 2024, testing both Continental and Pirelli models, but that test didn't include the then unreleased P Zero Race SL-R.

Pirelli launched its flagship P Zero Race SL-R tyre in March this year. The tyres use PAAS (Pirelli Advanced Aerodynamic System technology), which adds material to the sidewalls of the slick tyre to improve aerodynamic performance when mounted to a rim. Pirelli claimed rolling resistance and aero performance had improved considerably compared to its P Zero RACE RS model.
